title: Basic 8 · Subtract two images
summary: Arith a−b with op=sub — the standard 'what changed?' visualisation between two processings.

steps.title: Make a difference image
steps.body: Pixel-wise `a − b`. In cryo-EM a **before − after** diff visualises what changed after a processing step, or subtracts a background model from a particle. Same wiring as Basic 7 (Sum) with `op` switched from `add` to `sub`.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.clock` shows its image.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. Both source images now have previews.

steps.title: Wire Clock → a
steps.body: Drag from Clock's `image` to Arithmetic's `a`. Left operand (the one being subtracted from) = Clock.

steps.title: Wire Checker → b
steps.body: Drag from Checker's `image` to Arithmetic's `b`. Right operand (what gets subtracted) = Checker.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. With default `op=add` the result is Clock + Checker — a baseline before we switch the op to sub.

steps.title: Click Arithmetic
steps.body: Click the Arithmetic node. Change `op` in the Inspector.

steps.title: Set op to sub
steps.body: Change `op` to **`sub`**. Only the operator differs from `add` — the same node body is reused.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. Clock − Checker appears. Where Checker is white the Clock value is pushed down (dark); where Checker is black the Clock passes through — a clock face punched by a checkerboard.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body: To get a before-vs-after diff, wire: Clock → some processing → `sub.b` and Clock → `sub.a` (or reverse). `sub` produces signed values; negatives may be clipped to grey in the preview — Save to MRC for quantitative inspection.
